stages.name: Sales maximisation: sustainability risk
stages.title: Sales maximisation: sustainability risk
stages.sub: See why a firm producing at AC=AR has nothing spare to survive a shock.

steps.q: A firm producing where AC=AR earns only normal profit, just enough to keep resources in their current use. Is there any surplus profit left over above that minimum?
steps.right: No, there is nothing left over
steps.wrong: Yes, there is some left over
steps.hint: Normal profit is the minimum needed to stay in the market. What is left once that minimum is covered?
steps.pre: So a sales maximiser has no spare

steps.q: A firm with surplus profit above the minimum can save some of it inside the business for a difficult year. Can a firm with no surplus at all build up this kind of saved-up cash?
steps.right: No, it has nothing to set aside
steps.wrong: Yes, it can still save some
steps.hint: If every pound of revenue is already needed just to cover costs, is there anything left to store away?

steps.q: Costs suddenly rise, or sales unexpectedly fall for a while. With no saved-up cash to draw on, what happens to the firm financially?
steps.right: It struggles to cover its costs
steps.hint: With nothing extra held back, what happens the moment costs or revenue move against the firm?

steps.q: So compared to a firm holding back some surplus profit, how exposed is a sales maximiser when this kind of event hits?
steps.right: More exposed, it has no cushion to fall back on
steps.wrong: Equally exposed, the profit rule makes no difference
steps.hint: One firm has spare profit banked, the other does not. Which copes worse when things go wrong?
